doc.title: Michael Weiss interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 22, 2021

title: The pick-up motif in 'Atlantis'
summary: The motif Rowe noticed is the melody's pick-up bar, used to cue the next soloist after a vamp.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: This has been a wonderful conversation and I want to wrap up with something I heard last night of you playing at Small’s, a quartet with Steve Wilson. And I think you were playing a song called “Atlantis.” And I heard, I think, this little motif and I’ll try to hum it [scats]. And it came up every once in a while and it struck me like this is your way — forgive me if I’m making too much out of this, but it sounded like you were doing this with the idea of sort of marking a part in this performance and keeping the audience with you. That’s the way it struck me.

Well it’s just the pick-up bar of the melody. It’s the opening line of the song. It’s not the — it’s just the pick-up line into the melody, it’s not the melody per se, it’s just the opening into the melody. But let’s see, I think the way the form of the piece goes there was a little vamp section, there was the song form which was an open number of choruses for each soloist. And when the soloist plays his last chorus he cues into a little © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-
vamp section that’s four times. And at the end of that we used that pick-up of the melody to bring in the next soloist.
